summary: Global equity markets are displaying cautious optimism, with stocks ticking up modestly as investors navigate a complex geopolitical backdrop, though sentiment remains fragile given unresolved tensions across multiple fronts. The primary macro drivers this week center on upcoming U.S. inflation data, which will be critical in shaping Federal Reserve rate expectations, while oil markets are reacting sharply to Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, pushing crude prices nearly 2% higher. Energy stocks stand to benefit from elevated oil prices tied to Hormuz disruption fears, while gold has retreated slightly from a seven-week high as traders await inflation prints, and food-sector stocks face potential headwinds from tightening HHS oversight of food ingredients. The dominant risk factors include escalating Middle East tensions — particularly Iran's hardline leadership appointment of Mohsen Rezaei to its top security body, the stalled Gaza ceasefire framework, and continued Houthi military activity — all of which threaten to keep energy markets volatile and pressure risk appetite. In the short term, markets are likely to remain range-bound with an upward bias contingent on benign inflation data, but any further deterioration in Hormuz shipping lanes or a breakdown in Gaza negotiations could quickly reverse the recent equity recovery and drive defensive flows into gold and energy assets.
